**Non-blocking risk**: `isClaudeFixedSamplingModel` is consumed only by main-process `modelParameters.ts`. The shared-layer contract (§1.1) requires actual main and renderer consumers, so this adds main-only request policy to the cross-process API. Please keep the predicate private in `modelParameters.ts`, reusing the shared ID-normalization helpers. This is a non-blocking placement warning; no runtime failure was established from its current location.

comments.body:
**Pass with one gap.** I drove the real macOS app against a stand-in Anthropic endpoint that records what the app actually sends. With temperature turned on at 0.8, a chat message to `claude-opus-4-8` no longer carries `temperature`, `top_p` or `top_k` - exactly what this PR intends.

### What this PR changes

The rule "Claude rejects sampling params" widens from Opus 4.7-only to Opus 4.7+, Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.x, Fable and Mythos, and a custom `topK` is now dropped for the 5.5 models.

### How I tested it

1. Added a provider in the real app pointing at a local endpoint that logs the outgoing request body.
2. Turned on temperature (0.8) for the assistant.
3. Sent a message with **Claude Sonnet 4.6** (older model, should keep sampling params).
4. Sent a message with **Claude Opus 4.8** (newly covered model).

### Results

| Model | temperature in the outgoing request |
| --- | --- |
| `claude-sonnet-4-6` (baseline) | present, 0.8 |
| `claude-opus-4-8` | absent |

The baseline matters: the same temperature setting still reaches an older Claude model, so this is a targeted change and not a blanket removal of sampling params for all Claude models.

![Provider and models set up against the recording endpoint](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/blob/qa-evidence/docs/pr-evidence/21939/59fa8b0/s15-enabled.png?raw=true)

The service accepted the Sonnet 4.6 message and streamed a reply back, so the older path still works.

![Sonnet 4.6 message sent and answered](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/blob/qa-evidence/docs/pr-evidence/21939/59fa8b0/s42-sonnet-baseline.png?raw=true)

The Opus 4.8 message also completed, and its request body carried no sampling params.

![Opus 4.8 message sent](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/blob/qa-evidence/docs/pr-evidence/21939/59fa8b0/s44-opus-msg.png?raw=true)

### Not covered

- Real Anthropic production endpoints (no API key on this machine). The check above uses a local stand-in, so it proves what the app sends, not what Anthropic replies.
- Bedrock (`anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0`) and OpenRouter (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`) id forms - covered by your unit tests, not by a real chat here.
- `topP` and a custom `topK` were not exercised through the UI; the outgoing requests carried neither, so there was nothing to observe.

### Needed from you

Nothing blocking.

**Additional check on the 5.x branch of the new rule (same verdict: pass with the same gap).**

My earlier comment tested the Opus 4.8 branch of the widened rule. I repeated the same real-app setup for the **Claude 5 family** branch, which had not been exercised through a real chat yet:

| Model | temperature in the outgoing request |
| --- | --- |
| `claude-opus-5-qa` (newly covered 5.x naming) | absent |
| `claude-sonnet-4-6-qa` (older model, control) | present, 1.0 |

Both chats completed and streamed a reply, so chatting with a 5.x-named Claude model still works and only the sampling params are dropped.

![Opus 5-named model: message sent and answered](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/blob/qa-evidence/docs/pr-evidence/21939/59fa8b0/chat2-claude-opus-5-qa-reply.png?raw=true)

![Control Sonnet 4.6: message sent and answered](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/blob/qa-evidence/docs/pr-evidence/21939/59fa8b0/chat2-claude-sonnet-4-6-qa-reply.png?raw=true)

Uncovered is unchanged: real Anthropic production endpoints (no API key on this machine) and the Bedrock/OpenRouter id forms (unit-test only).

Nothing blocking.
